questions.prompt: What is a limitation critics describe in current contrast mathematics?

options.text: It requires text to be extremely small to pass.
It treats light text on a dark background exactly the same as dark text on a light background.
It only measures the color red.
It automatically fails any design that uses brand colors.

questions.explanation: Current math is not polarity-aware, meaning it does not model how human eyes perceive reverse polarity.
questions.hint: Think about how it handles inverting colors.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Recognize the limitations critics describe in current contrast mathematics.

questions.prompt: What does it mean for a contrast algorithm to be polarity-aware?

options.text: It only works in freezing temperatures.
It uses different math depending on whether the text is lighter or darker than the background.
It evaluates the emotional impact of a color palette.
It only evaluates black and white designs.

questions.explanation: A polarity-aware model understands that light-on-dark is visually different from dark-on-light, modeling human vision more accurately.
questions.hint: It relates to which color is on top and which is on the bottom.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand how color polarity affects human perception.

questions.prompt: How does the proposed Accessible Perceptual Contrast Algorithm (APCA) handle font size?

options.text: It dictates that all fonts must be 12 pixels.
It is spatially aware, generating scores that dictate how thick or large a font must be for a specific color pair.
It forces mobile devices to zoom in automatically.

questions.explanation: APCA ties contrast scores directly to specific font weights and sizes, recognizing that physical size impacts readability.
questions.hint: Think about how it pairs color scores with typography details.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Learn about perceptual contrast approaches being explored.
